lastPrompt: This repository implements four graduate-level machine-learning programming assignments covering supervised learning, randomized optimization, unsupervised learning and dimensionality reduction, and reinforcement learning on MDPs. The framework uses scikit-learn classifiers, clustering algorithms, dimensionality reduction techniques, and mdptoolbox for MDP-based RL environments. Your working directory is `/workspace`. The project code is already present. You need to implement all the modules and features listed below so that all tests pass. Implement the following modules: The following modules need to be implemented or substantially built out: A1-SL (Supervised Learning) (`A1-SL/`): This module contains training pipelines for multiple classifiers — Decision Tree, k-Nearest Neighbors, Support Vector Machine, Neural Network, and Boosted Tree. Each classifier module handles hyperparameter grid search via cross-validation, model fitting, ROC-AUC scoring on train/test sets, and optional model complexity/validation curve generation. The shared utility module provides data loading with scaling, validation curve computation, learning curve plotting, grid search export, and specialized visualizations. (~7 files, ~10 functions to implement) A3-USL (Unsupervised Learning & Dimensionality Reduction) (`A3-USL/`): This module implements K-Means and Expectation-Maximization clustering pipelines with comprehensive metric evaluation, plus four dimensionality reduction techniques (PCA, ICA, Random Projection, Locally Linear Embedding) with reconstruction error analysis. The clustering module benchmarks estimators across varying cluster counts, computing quality metrics and generating comparison visualizations. (~2 files, ~8 functions to implement) A4-MDPs (Markov Decision Processes) (`A4-MDPs/`): This module implements Policy Iteration on forest management MDPs. The run_episodes function simulates a Forest MDP under a fixed policy, handling fire probability, state transitions, and reward accumulation. The run_forest function runs the full PI pipeline across parameter grids and generates heatmap visualizations of rewards, iterations, and runtimes. (~1 file, ~2 functions to implement) The tests also depend on these signatures and entry points: The following functions are called directly by the test suite.
